Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Ms. Manpreet Kaur, learned counsel with Mr.
Sanjay Kumar Chandel, learned counsel for the
respondent no.3.
4. Mr. Harjeet Singh, the petitioner, is present
through video conferencing, duly identified by Mr.
Harshpal Sekhon, Advocate.
5. Ms. Randeep Kaur, respondent no. 3, is present
through video conferencing, duly identified by Ms.
Manpreet Kaur, Advocate.
6. By means of the present petition, the petitioner
has sought quashing of the F.I.R. No. 326 of 2024, dated
06.12.2024, under Sections 323, 354, 498-A, 506 of the
Indian Penal Code & Section 3/4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961, registered at Police Station- I.T.I.,

District- Udham Singh Nagar, lodged by the respondent
no. 3/ Randeep Kaur.
7. Compounding Application (IA No. 1 of 2026) has
been filed on behalf of the petitioner and also signed by
the respondent no. 3 as well, in which a prayer has been
made for compounding of the entire proceedings arising
out of the F.I.R. No. 326 of 2024, dated 06.12.2024,
under Sections 323, 354, 498-A, 506 of the Indian Penal
Code & Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961,
registered at Police Station- I.T.I., District- Udham
Singh Nagar, lodged by the respondent no. 3/ Randeep
Kaur.
8. On an interaction with the respondent no. 3, who
is appearing through video conferencing, she states that
she has settled the matter with the petitioner and she
does not want to pursue the matter any further. In the
affidavit also, the respondent no. 3 has categorically
stated that due to irreparable breakdown of marriage,
spouses have decided to part ways in order to put an
quietus to the dispute. As a matter of fact, one-time
settlement amount has been paid by the petitioner to the
complainant. Divorce petition under Section 27 of the
Uniform Civil Code of Uttarakhand has been moved.
Now, the parties have reached an amicable settlement
and have settled their disputes. Therefore, present
Criminal Petition along with Compounding Application
is being filed. The parties do not want criminal
proceedings to continue and, therefore, request this
Court to kindly interfere.
9. On an interaction with the petitioner, he also
makes a similar averment that the matter has been

settled and the proceedings qua him deserve to be
quashed. An affidavit has also been filed on behalf of
the petitioner on the similar lines as has been filed by
the respondent no. 3.
10. The learned counsel for the petitioner and the
respondent no. 3 would submit that the parties have
resolved their disputes amicably and the respondent no.
3 does not wish to prosecute the petitioner any further,
and therefore, permitting the further continuance of the
criminal proceedings would be a futile exercise.
11. The learned AGA for the State would submit that
the matter emanates out of a matrimonial dispute and the
offences can be compounded.
12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of "B.S.
Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another",
(2003) 4 SCC 675, "Nikhil Merchant vs. CBI and
another", (2008) 9 SCC 650 and "Gian Singh vs. State
of Punjab", 2012 (10) SCC 303 as well as in Transfer
Petition (Criminal) No. 115 of 2012 (Dimpey Gujral vs.
Union Territory of Chandigarh) decided on 06.12.2012,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court has permitted the
compounding of non-compoundable offence and has
held that in exercise of power under Section 482 of
Cr.P.C., compounding can be done in non-compoundable offences.
13. In such view of the matter, since the parties to the
matrimony have resolved their disputes amicably, and
the respondent no. 2 has categorically stated before this
Court, appearing through VC, that she does not want to
further prosecute the petitioner, therefore, letting the

matter go into trial would be a futile exercise.
14. In such view of the matter, Compounding
Application deserves to be allowed, and the proceedings
arising out of the F.I.R. No. 326 of 2024, dated
06.12.2024, under Sections 323, 354, 498-A, 506 of the
Indian Penal Code & Section 3/4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961, registered at Police Station- I.T.I.,
District- Udham Singh Nagar, lodged by the respondent
no. 3/ Randeep Kaur, qua the petitioner are hereby
quashed.
15. The Compounding Application (IA No. 1 of 2026)
is allowed accordingly.
16. The writ petition is disposed of accordingly qua
the petitioner.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
06.11.2026
Shiv/
